captions_on_screen: text boxes (not speech subtitles): 1-3 lines of white text in the centre of the frame, no background box; a new text every 1.3 s in step with the cuts for most of the video

ending_and_cta: Last 3 s: close-up of the elephant spraying water, then fading to dark, with text 'רוצות גם? / הגיבו ״יוקידו״ / לקבלת קישור למשחק'. Caption CTA: write 'יוקידו' in the comments to receive a purchase link by message.
price_or_code: no figure shown; the text says the price is accessible ('המחיר הנגיש'); the link is sent to commenters who write 'יוקידו'
convincing: Interpretation: short (17 s), one idea per text box, every benefit is visibly demonstrated with water, a clear one-word comment CTA; the toy is cute and colourful and the first frame already shows the brand on the box.
weak_or_overproduced: Interpretation: no speech and no personal reaction to the toy; the child's face is never shown; the 'accessible price' claim has no figure; the text appears fast (about 1.3 s each) so a viewer may not finish reading; the disclosure is a short caption line at the end.
lumebook_lesson: Interpretation: the 'comment a word and I send the link' CTA with a one-word code word, text in step with cuts, and an under-20-second demo can be recreated with a phone. For a book, the equivalent demonstration is showing the child's name appearing on the cover and in pages in 1-1.5 s cuts. A hands-only version avoids needing a child's face.
solo_without_child: partly: the box and sprinkling shots can be filmed by an adult alone; the child-hands shots (about a third) need a child
not_verified: Whether any music is present (inferred from the absence of speech and the transcript artifact); whether Palphot sells the toy or paid for the post (only 'בשיתוף' in the caption, paid-partnership label 0); the purchase price; the ages of the children (hands only, no faces); the comment-reply flow.
